title: Chapter 1 · Lighting the First Fire
subtitle: Simmer, sear or plate - three ways to feed five races

states.label: Flavor
states.description: How good the cooking itself is - heat and seasoning

states.label: Craving
states.description: How badly the smell and the look make you want a bite

states.label: Bond
states.description: How much the meal warmed the ones eating it

scenes.title: You fell into another world - the pot made it too
scenes.description: A crack in the clouds swallowed you and a small cooking pot together. You wake up in a forest where the light smells like honey, and there's a little slime in front of you that's so hungry it's nearly melting.

actions.name: Boil a pot of hot soup first
actions.hint: You have a pot, you have water - leave the rest to the fire

soup.text: Wild scallions, mushrooms, and one small piece of jelly the slime dropped itself, all brought to a boil. After it drinks, its body turns from half-transparent to a warm amber - and then it follows you.

scenes.title: An elf's dew pancake - unchanged for three hundred years
scenes.description: An elf in the Silverleaf forest hands you a pancake so thin you can see through it, and says very politely, "This is the whole of our cuisine." Her ears droop as she says it.

actions.name: Drizzle honey and simmer it low
actions.hint: Let the sweetness sink into every layer

actions.name: Pan-fry it until the edges catch
actions.hint: A browned edge is a flavour switch

simmer.text: The honey turns into small amber bubbles in the pan, and the pancake goes soft and glossy as it drinks them up. The elf takes one bite, says nothing for a long moment, then asks, very quietly, "Could I... have another one?"

sear.text: A fine sizzle starts along the pan's edge and the pancake curls into a golden-brown rim - crisp first, then soft. The whole Silverleaf forest can smell something it has never smelled before.

plate.text: The petals go on ring by ring, finished with a pinch of crushed toasted nuts. The elf holds it up to the moonlight for a long time, turns it three times, and still can't bring herself to take a bite.

scenes.title: A dwarf's stone mushroom - knock it and it rings
scenes.description: A dwarf sets an underground mushroom on the cutting board and taps it with a hammer. It rings, clear as a bell. "Our family has eaten it this way for generations," he says, perfectly serious, with perfectly good teeth.

actions.name: Lid on, simmer it for three hours
Slice it thin and sear it hard
actions.hint: Thin enough to see through, and it can't stay tough

actions.name: Grind it to flour and bake bread

simmer.text: The lid rattles for a long time, and the mushroom ends up springy as well-stewed tendon. The dwarf wipes one eye with his beard and insists it was the steam.

sear.text: The moment the slices hit the pan there's a burst of toasted aroma, the edges curling into little waves. One bite crackles, then melts on your tongue. The whole mine is quietly swallowing.

plate.text: The mushroom flour goes into dough and comes out as a batch of dark round loaves; break one open and the steam pours out, the crumb soft enough to leave a fingerprint. The dwarf carves the recipe into the mine wall on the spot.

scenes.title: The orcs' campfire - always cooked past done
scenes.description: The orc tribe's roast is black outside and raw inside. They've eaten it this way for years and insist it's "the taste of a warrior". A small orc secretly shaves off the burnt part before daring a first bite.

actions.name: Bank the fire down and cook it low
Marinate it in herbs overnight
actions.hint: Let the flavour move in first

actions.name: Cut it small, one skewer each

simmer.text: The fire drops to red coals and the meat slowly turns to something that gives juice at a touch. The chief cuts in and freezes - even pink all the way through, not a hint of raw, juice running down the blade.

sear.text: Rosemary, garlic and a little honey form a shining shell on the surface, hissing the moment the flame licks it. The smell goes up over the treetops, and the next tribe over comes asking what's cooking.

plate.text: The meat is cut small and threaded onto twigs, one skewer each, so nobody has to fight for the last piece. The little orcs line up and, for the first time, finish a meal in complete quiet.

scenes.title: A halfling's afternoon tea - the sugar jar is empty
scenes.description: Halflings eat four meals a day and the fourth is afternoon tea. Today there's a crisis: the sugar jar is down to the bottom. Every round door in the village is open, and everyone is worrying together.

actions.name: Simmer a pot of berry sugar
actions.hint: Sweetness can be made at home

actions.name: Roast a honeycomb for wild honey
actions.hint: The wild bees keep the better stock

actions.name: Stack a tower of little pancakes

simmer.text: The berries bubble and bubble in the small pot and slowly reduce into a thick purple-red syrup that spreads in slow lines across a hot pancake, dyeing the whole thing violet.

sear.text: Once the honeycomb is roasted the honey comes out on its own - golden, stringy, with a whisper of smoke. The halflings lick their spoons clean, then very solemnly lick them a second time.

plate.text: The little pancakes stack up into a tower with one whole red berry on top. Everyone claps first and eats second - even the bees outside stop on the glass to look.

scenes.title: The lost walking pudding in the maze
scenes.description: There are no monsters on the seventh floor of the stone maze - only a pudding, walking back and forth. It follows you for a long time, then says in a small voice that it wants to go home but can't remember where home is.

actions.name: Cook hot soup and think with it
actions.hint: Memories get warmed out of you

actions.name: Make a dessert that looks like it

simmer.text: The soup goes down and the pudding slowly returns to a pale caramel colour. Then it jumps up: home is behind that leaking stone wall over there. It bounces ahead of you the whole way.

sear.text: The dropped jelly melts into syrup in the pan and cools into translucent shards that crackle - sweet, exactly right. The pudding watches its own pieces become snacks and puffs up with pride.

plate.text: You make a tiny pudding in its exact shape and pour caramel over it. It hugs the dessert and says this tastes like home - then leads you out of the maze.

scenes.title: The dragon's castle - no fire lit for centuries
scenes.description: A silver dragon guards a hall of gold and silver and hasn't eaten a hot meal in hundreds of years. Tonight the elves, dwarves, orcs and halflings have all come. The long table holds one small pot - and the whole treasury.

actions.name: One slow pot with every race's ingredients
actions.hint: Cook together, or it isn't eating together

actions.name: Ask the dragon for one breath of fire
actions.hint: There's only one stove like this in the world

simmer.text: Elven honey, dwarven mushrooms, orc roast and halfling syrup slowly flow into the same pot. The dragon brings its whole face down to the rim and says nothing for a long time, tapping the floor with its tail.

sear.text: The dragon breathes for one second and the surface of the pot sets into a beautiful caramel shell. When it's cracked open the steam rushes out and every race in the room makes the same sound at once.

plate.text: The three tiers stack up as mushroom bread, honey-glazed roast and berry pudding, with a little flag made from a spatula on top. The dragon walks three full circles around it before daring a first bite.

endings.title: Meowchelin Three Stars · The Kitchen Opens
endings.description: The dragon gives up the brightest floor of the castle. The elves handle sweets, the dwarves handle heat, the orcs handle skewers, the halflings handle eating four times a day - and you are the chef, spatula tucked at your waist. Three stars hang over the door, polished from an old pot bottom.

endings.title: The Smell That Queued a Continent
endings.description: The smell went over the mountain and past the Silverleaf forest. By the next morning the queue outside the castle reached the far shore of the lake. The dragon keeps order and reminds everyone every twenty minutes: no cutting in line, no rushing the pot.

endings.title: Home Cooking That Warms You Through
endings.description: No opening ceremony, no signboard. The dwarves carried in their own benches, the elves brought honey, the orcs keep the fire, and the halflings come four times a day. You just cook one pot of soup - whoever walks in gets a bowl first and talks afterwards.
